title: Projects
text:
Examines how demographic sorting into offshorable occupations evolved during U.S. service-sector offshoring expansion, 2001–2019. Using ACS microdata linked to Autor-Dorn offshorability scores, OLS with state and year fixed effects reveals persistent nativity and education gradients in offshoring exposure and an unevenly distributed wage penalty.




Classifies U.S. workers into high and low cognitive demand occupations using 2019 ACS microdata linked to O*NET skill ratings, comparing logistic regression, LASSO, and XGBoost across 800,000 observations. All three models converge on education credentials and industry as dominant predictors, with persistent racial gaps after conditioning on observable characteristics.




Contingent valuation study estimating willingness to pay among Oregon and Washington residents for thermal discharge regulation on the Columbia River. Uses dichotomous choice CV methodology and logit regression following Hanemann (1984) to recover WTP estimates, with analysis of protest zero responses and embedding effects.




Proposes a coordinated federal reform package for coal ash (CCR) management, addressing asymmetric information, deferred liability, and weak enforcement. Combines third-party monitoring, incentive-compatible financial assurance, strengthened closure standards, and mandatory reuse targets to correct a compounding market failure.




Analyzes the ASP+6% Part B drug reimbursement formula as a principal-agent problem that will undercut Medicare’s 2028 price negotiations. As negotiated prices fall, the add-on shrinks, pushing physicians toward costlier, non-negotiated substitutes. Recommends replacing the percentage add-on with a tiered flat rate by drug class.

title: Projects
text:

Environmental Deregulation, Emissions Intensity, and Firm Behavior: Evidence from American Industries (In Progress)
Tests Pigouvian vs. Coasian predictions on how U.S. industrial emissions intensity responds to federal environmental deregulation, using facility-level EPA emissions data linked to firm financials and patent records. Applies heterogeneity-robust staggered DiD (Callaway-Sant’Anna, Sun-Abraham) and synthetic control methods to estimate effects across a small number of treated industries, with a direct test of the Porter Hypothesis using R&D and patenting activity to identify mechanism.

title: Ireland Gomes
text:
I’m an economist holding an M.Sc Economics and B.S. Economics with minors in legal studies and mathematics, both from the University of Oregon.
I believe economics is where you’re most likely to find the beginning of any problem’s solution. Theory to make sense of it, empirics to test it, and together, the most rigorous and versatile toolkit there is for driving real change.
My work spans microeconomic theory, applied microeconomics, econometric theory, econometric applications, and machine learning. Within my applicative work, I draw on methods including difference-in-differences (DiD), two-way fixed effects (TWFE), event studies, regression discontinuity (RD), instrumental variables (IVs), penalized regression, debiased ML, and ensemble methods, among others.
While being an academic at heart, areas of particular professional interest to me are forensic litigation, regulatory economics, program evaluation, policy analysis, quantitaive research & risk modeling. Alongside are my research interests that include industrial organization, labor economics, information economics, antitrust & competition, public economics, regulation, and policy.
